To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the vanishing of all tree-level on-shell scattering amplitudes is a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a nonlinear transformation that maps a given field theory onto a free field theory and that the vanishing at one loop of all on-shell scattering amptudes requires the introduction of a field-dependent wave function renormalization.

all theories with derivative interactions, which are locally related to a theory with vanishing S -matrix, can be transformed to a theory with a vanishing S -mass, and that all theories with vanishing S-matrix are locally related to the free theory.

all on-shell scattering amplitudes of a scalar field theory vanish if the theory is invariant under a nonlinear field redefinition and that a field-dependent renormalization of the wave function can be used to cancel one-loop divergences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a class of scalar field theories with a nontrivial classical structure, which nevertheless are free at the quantum level.
the structure of scalar theories having the property of vanishing tree-level S -matrix elements.
the structure of scalar theories with derivative coupling, which we call “nullifying theories”.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vanishing of all on-shell S-matrix elements in tree approximation is a very strong and highly non-trivial condition, which, however, does not necessarily imply a free theory.
there are no one-loop counterterms in these theories.
the vanishing of all on-shell S-matrix elements in tree approximation is not in itself sufficient for the proof of a theory's triviality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
all theories having derivative interactions, and which have the property that all tree amplitudes vanish, are locally related to a theory with a free field.

the existence of a large class of scalar theories with vanishing on-shell S -matrices is a consequence of the existence of a nonlinear transformation that relates the theory in question to a free field theory, and the existence of such a nonlinear transformation is a consequence of a nontrivial structure of the field space of the theory.
all theories having the property of vanishing on-shell S - matrix elements in tree approximation can be related to a free scalar theory by a field-dependent wavefunction renormalization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of derivative couplings in a theory is not necessarily an indication that the theory has a non-trivial S -matrix.
the presence of derivative couplings does not necessarily lead to nontrivial S -matrix elements.
, at the one-loop order, the S -matrix of a theory with derivative couplings is not a unique function of the couplings, but rather depends also on the choice of the field-dependent renormalization.
